findings.current: At Xixia, Sama Pyo confronts Shaolin’s young Martial Uncle, the scarred and hoarse-voiced Unnamed, over the Black Dragon Saber.
findings.defect: The summary treats Black Dragon Saber, Sama Pyo’s sobriquet, as the disputed weapon and places the encounter at Xixia despite the chapter locating it in Henan.
findings.rationale: Chapter 515 identifies Sama Pyo as Black Dragon Saber, has Unnamed order him to return the merchant’s sword, and explicitly states that they are in Henan.
findings.replacement: At a ferry landing in Henan, Sama Pyo confronts Shaolin’s young Martial Uncle, the scarred and hoarse-voiced Unnamed, after taking a merchant’s sword.

findings.current: He later reunites with Unnamed, recognizes Jung Ho as his former Garam Middle School classmate Park Jung Ho, and learns that Shaolin’s new Abbot—Unnamed’s eldest Senior Brother—wants to meet him.
findings.defect: The summary records Taekyung’s groggy joke and mistaken association as a genuine recognition of Jung Ho.
findings.rationale: In Chapter 516, Taekyung asks whether Jung Ho is his old classmate before fully waking, then realizes that the monk is Shaolin’s Discipline Hall Master; the text never confirms that they are the same person.
findings.replacement: He later reunites with Unnamed, sleepily mistakes Jung Ho for his former Garam Middle School classmate Park Jung Ho, and learns that Shaolin’s new Abbot—Unnamed’s eldest Senior Brother—wants to meet him.

findings.current: Jung Ho is Park Jung Ho, Taekyung’s former Garam Middle School classmate, and Shaolin’s Discipline Hall Master.
findings.defect: A momentary joke is promoted into a false identity claim.
findings.rationale: Nothing in Chapters 515–519 establishes Jung Ho as Taekyung’s former classmate, and Jung Ho responds with confusion to the suggestion.
findings.replacement: Jung Ho is Shaolin’s Discipline Hall Master; while still half asleep, Taekyung briefly mistakes him for his former Garam Middle School classmate Park Jung Ho.

findings.current: Their clash coincides with a Dark Heaven assault, sending the gathered Murim forces into battle.
findings.defect: No Dark Heaven assault occurs; the duel’s destruction and Supreme Peak qi are mistakenly interpreted as one.
findings.rationale: Chapters 518–519 reveal that the supposed attack was Jeok Cheongang and Nangong Cheon’s duel, followed by a cascading misidentification.
findings.replacement: Their clash destroys the inn and is mistaken for a Dark Heaven assault, sending the gathered Murim forces charging toward the scene.

findings.current: Dark Heaven attacked near the Alliance gathering. Jeok’s emergence from the burning inn caused a chaotic misidentification; the assault’s broader consequences remain to be seen.
findings.defect: The continuity record asserts an attack that the reading copies explicitly reveal never occurred and leaves invented consequences open.
findings.rationale: The disturbance originates entirely from the promised duel; no Dark Heaven combatants or separate assault appear in the packet.
findings.replacement: Jeok Cheongang and Nangong Cheon’s duel near the Alliance gathering was mistaken for a Dark Heaven attack. Jeok’s emergence from the burning inn caused a chaotic misidentification before Nangong Cheon helped end the confrontation.

findings.current: The Dark Heaven assault near Mount Song has ended in a chaotic misunderstanding: Jeok Cheongang emerged from a burning inn, was mistaken for a Dark Heaven fiend, was identified as the Returned-to-Youth Fire King by Peng Cheolhu, and was separated from the mob by Nangong Cheon.
findings.defect: The active state preserves the nonexistent Dark Heaven assault as fact and obscures that the entire disturbance began with Jeok Cheongang’s duel against Nangong Cheon.
findings.rationale: Durable state must distinguish the characters’ temporary misunderstanding from established continuity or future chapters will inherit a false attack.
findings.replacement: Jeok Cheongang’s duel with Nangong Cheon near Mount Song destroyed an inn and was mistaken for a Dark Heaven assault. Jeok emerged from the burning wreckage, was mistaken for a Dark Heaven fiend, was eventually identified as the Returned-to-Youth Fire King, and was separated from the mob after Nangong Cheon intervened.

findings.defect: “Tarnation” is a dated, sanitized euphemism that clashes with Taekyung’s contemporary and routinely profane narrative voice.
findings.rationale: The surrounding chapters consistently give Taekyung direct modern profanity; the current expression sounds like an imported Western rustic affectation.
findings.source: Chapter 518, Taekyung observing the distant explosions

findings.current: You’re a kid whose blood hasn’t even dried on his head, yet you keep talking back to me…
findings.defect: The image is an unnatural Korean idiom calque in English dialogue.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the accusation of extreme youth and insolence while sounding natural in contemporary English.
findings.replacement: You’re still wet behind the ears, yet you keep talking back to me…
findings.source: Chapter 519, Thunderbolt Saber King arguing with Taekyung

summary: The reading copies remain coherent overall, but the checkpoint summary and durable state contain repeated factual errors: Sama Pyo’s sobriquet is treated as an object, Taekyung’s sleepy joke about Jung Ho is recorded as a genuine recognition, and Jeok Cheongang’s duel is misreported as an actual Dark Heaven assault. Two conspicuous Korean-style or dated expressions also break Taekyung’s established English voice.
